'''''Narcissus bulbocodium''''', the '''petticoat daffodil'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=NABU|taxon=Narcissus bulbocodium|accessdate=28 January 2016}}</ref> or '''hoop-petticoat daffodil''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Amaryllidaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern and western [[France]], [[Portugal]], and [[Spain]]. Some sources say that the species is also native to [[Morocco]], but this is based on populations formerly thought to be varieties of ''N. bulbocodium'' but now regarded as separate species.<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=282778 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>

== Description ==
''Narcissus bulbocodium'' is a variable, small, [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]] [[bulbous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]], growing to {{convert|10|-|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall, with grass-like leaves, and deep yellow trumpet-shaped flowers in mid-Spring. The flower is unusual in that the central trumpet (corona) is exceptionally large in relation to the outer section (perianth) consisting of tiny pointed segments.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-L encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>
The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''bulbocodium'' means "woolly bulb".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358308#page/301/mode/1up Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753. Species Plantarum 1: 289]</ref> At 12 mm it has the smallest floral diameter amongst ''Narcissus''.

==Hybrids==
''Narcissus bulbocodium'' is a parent of several [[Hybrid (biology)#Hybrid plants|hybrid]]s, including:<ref>{{cite web|title=International Plant Names Index (IPNI) - ''Narcissus bulbocodium''|url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do;jsessionid=C5EE37A57A03C9D7799BE6E780FBA3CD?id=65939-1&back_page=%2Fipni%2FeditSimplePlantNameSearch.do%3Bjsessionid%3DC5EE37A57A03C9D7799BE6E780FBA3CD%3Ffind_wholeName%3DNarcissus%2Bbulbocodium%26output_format%3Dnormal|accessdate=25 May 2013}}</ref>
*''N.'' × ''abilioi'' Fern.Casas (''N. bulbocodium'' × ''[[Narcissus jonquilla|N. jonquilla]]'')
*''N.'' × ''brevitubulosus'' A.Fern. (''N. bulbocodium'' × ''[[Narcissus asturiensis|N. asturiensis]]'')
*''N.'' × ''montcaunicus'' Fern.Casas (''N. bulbocodium'' × ''[[Narcissus eugeniae|N. eugeniae]]'')
*''N.'' × ''lopezii'' Fern.Casas (''[[Narcissus obvallaris|N. obvallaris]]'' × ''N. bulbocodium'')
*''N.'' × ''rozeirae'' Fern.Casas & Pérez-Chisc. (''N. bulbocodium'' × ''[[Narcissus pallidulus|N. pallidulus]]'')
*''N.'' × ''barrae'' Fern.Casas (''[[Narcissus cantabricus|N. cantabricus]]'' 'Redouté' × ''N. bulbocodium'')

==Cultivation==
''Narcissus bulbocodium'' is widely planted in gardens, and can be naturalised in grass. It requires relatively dry conditions during the summer dormant period, so is suitable for planting beneath [[deciduous]] trees.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dusoir|first=Rory|title=How to grow: the hoop-petticoat daffodil|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/howtogrow/3309935/How-to-grow-the-hoop-petticoat-daffodil.html|work=The Telegraph|date=5 April 2003 |accessdate=24 May 2013}}</ref>  Numerous [[variety (botany)|varieties]] and [[cultivars]] exist, including ''N. bulbocodium'' subsp. ''bulbocodium'' [[var.]] ''conspicuus'' (pale yellow flowers) and 'Golden Bells', a vigorous cultivar with long-lasting deep yellow flowers.<ref name=RHSAZ />

''Narcissus bulbocodium'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Narcissus bulbocodium''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/11348/Narcissus-bulbocodium-(13)/Details | accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> <!-- AGM withdrawn as have the Golden Bells Group <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/233991/Narcissus-bulbocodium-Golden-Bells-Group-(10)/Details | title = ''Narcissus bulbocodium'' Golden Bells group | publisher = RHS | accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> and ''N. bulbocodium'' subsp. ''bulbocodium'' var. ''citrinus''.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/74848/Narcissus-bulbocodium-subsp-bulbocodium-var-citrinus-(13)/Details
